chunks: Then in their train We sent Our apostles, and succeeding them Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and put into the hearts of his followers compassion and. But they created monasticism which had not been prescribed for them by Us except for seeking the pleasure of God; yet they did not observe it as it should have been rightly observed. So We gave those among them who were believers their reward; but most of them are disobedient.

key_terms.أَجْرَهُمْ: Their reward; given to the believers among the followers of Jesus.
key_terms.ابْتَدَعُوهَا: They invented/created it; referring to the self-invented nature of monasticism.
key_terms.رَهْبَانِيَّةٌ: Monasticism; a state of religious devotion or celibacy, here described as an innovation.
key_terms.رِضْوَانِ اللَّهِ: The pleasure of God; the motive for introducing monasticism.
key_terms.فَمَا رَعَوْهَا: Yet they did not observe it; indicating failure to adhere to the practice properly.

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and nature of monasticism (Rahbaniyyah) according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for understanding the evolution of divine guidance, where Jesus (peace be upon him) serves as the seal of the previous prophetic cycle, bringing the Injil to restore the Torah's essence. The term 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) is interpreted not merely as asceticism but as an innovation by his followers to seek divine pleasure, which they ultimately failed to uphold with fidelity, leading to a dichotomy between the faithful who received their reward and the majority who became disobedient.
